log.reply:
**Subject: Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments**

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation summary**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Profile Block records three AI use cases: a deployed customer service chatbot on the support portal, an AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line and AI sales forecasting planned for next year. AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The listed regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target with work to start next year. An internal audit finding from June 2026 records no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

**What the Briefing covers for the Client**

The Briefing will map the EU AI Act and GDPR to the three use cases as expectations to verify with counsel. This includes transparency expectations for the chatbot and the question of whether the visual inspection system falls within a higher-risk category. United States expectations will appear only as a general landscape item because no US driver is listed. The readiness discussion will address the audit finding, the constraint that customer data must stay in the EU and the requirement to consult the German works council before anything touches production staff.

We will outline a governance operating model using the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Board-layer points will draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). We will also explore how this model might connect to the listed incumbent frameworks: ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, ISO 9001 quality management system and the internal audit function. Three principles guide the session: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. The Briefing does not promise certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

**Logistics and price**

The Briefing runs for two hours, live and virtual, for executive leadership and board-level attendees. The listed audience roles are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The session date is Unknown and will be agreed together. The price is US$3,000.

**What the Client receives afterward**

The Client will receive a written summary of the decisions surfaced, readiness observations and implementation priorities, with framework references and open questions to take to counsel.

**Next step**

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. At intake, please confirm the attendee list, a session date, which incumbent framework processes you consider relevant to AI and whether the visual inspection pilot processes personal data.

Kind regards,

Senior AI Governance Consultant
AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: Word count: I included the subject line, headings, salutation, sign-off and closing line, and counted URLs as single words. The result is about 441 and no plausible counting method reaches 451, but a different tokenizer could land a few words away from mine.

"The Client will receive a written summary of the decisions surfaced, readiness observations and implementation priorities..." is a post-Briefing deliverable the prompt does not define for Mode A. I treated it as proposed work, not a Client fact. Another scorer could read it as an invented program element, but it is not a fact about the Client.
"Your stated objective is..." attributes the quote to the Sponsor. The block attributes it to Dana Whitfield, so I treated it as stated, not inferred.

Including the audit finding, the data-residency constraint and the works council requirement in the readiness discussion is proposed work. It does not assert how these relate to any Client system or person, so I did not treat it as an inferred relation under Guardrail 6.
"transparency expectations for the chatbot" is general EU AI Act landscape content framed for verification with counsel, not a Client fact.
